rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so this experiment tests a multimodal configuration combining scgpt (RNA) and imagenet_vit_l (image) with weighted fusion, which are strong baselines. This clarifies the potential of multimodal approaches early in the search. It is the best use of the first experiment to establish a baseline for further exploration.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l) achieves 0.54 accuracy. This experiment tests config_009, which uses resnet50 instead of imagenet_vit_l for images. This clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on performance, a critical design decision. It balances exploration of key components while building on the multimodal foundation of the first experiment.

The existing evidence shows that using scgpt RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with weighted fusion achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests changing the aggregation method from avgpool (used in config_001) to transformer, which could improve performance by better capturing interactions between modalities. This clarifies whether aggregation method is a critical factor, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing components with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and switching fusion from weighted to concat, which could clarify if these changes improve performance. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives (critical for multimodal performance) while maintaining core components (scgpt RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation). This reduces uncertainty about the image encoder's impact on accuracy without deviating too far from the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with the same image encoder and fusion method, clarifying if the RNA encoder choice is critical. It balances exploration (testing a different RNA encoder) with exploitation (keeping other high-performing components unchanged).

The existing evidence shows config_026 (0.706 accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the high-performing RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion. It clarifies if transformer aggregation improves upon the current best, exploiting the promising direction of scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.724989 in config_027). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 while retaining scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) impacts performance, leveraging the strong foundation of scvi_n200 and transformer-based fusion.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other components the same) could improve performance. It clarifies the impact of fusion strategy on accuracy, leveraging the strong foundation of the current top performer.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_027) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could clarify if combining resnet50 with scgpt improves performance. It balances exploration of image encoder alternatives while maintaining high-performing fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder (e.g., config_027 with 0.724989 accuracy) outperform others. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder (untested combination) and weighted fusion, which could potentially improve accuracy. It clarifies whether resnet50 is better than imagenet_vit_l for image encoding when paired with scvi_n200, leveraging the strong performance of scvi_n200 while exploring a new image encoder.
